chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about one who forgot to wipe his head until he stood in the salat (prayer). He said: "He should turn away and wipe his head and his feet."

Then he said, may Allah the Exalted support him: if he leaves that until what he had performed wudu (ablution) upon from his limbs dries, he repeats the wudu anew so that his wudu may be consecutive and not disjointed. So that which indicates this is as follows.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the salat (prayer) in which he had already stood
key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: the wudu (ablution) that must be repeated if continuity is broken
key_terms.جَوَارِحِهِ: his limbs that were previously washed or wiped in wudu
key_terms.رَأْسَهُ: his head, the part to be wiped in wudu
key_terms.رِجْلَيْهِ: his feet, which are to be wiped in this context
key_terms.يَمْسَحَ: to wipe as part of wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he forgets to wipe his head in wudu until he has stood for salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who forgets to wipe the head during wudu (ablution) and only remembers after standing for salat (prayer). If the lapse is noticed before the moisture of the previously washed limbs dries, he completes the missing wiping; otherwise, he must restart the wudu so that it remains continuous.
